newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schmidt attacks Tietmeyer on EMU; BUBA no comment.
newsitem.headline: Schmidt attacks Tietmeyer on EMU; BUBA no comment.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Thursday declined to comment on sharp criticism by former German Chancellor Helmut Schmidt who said the central bank's president Hans Tietmeyer was endangering European monetary union.

A Bundesbank spokesman said Schmidt had levelled similar accusations against Tietmeyer earlier this year. "The Bundesbank is opposed to dealing with these accusations again," the spokesman said in response to a Reuter enquiry.
Schmidt, in an open letter published in Thursday's edition of German newspaper Die Zeit, said he regarded Tietmeyer as the most important opponent of European monetary union.

He called Tietmeyer's insistence on strict adherence to the Maastricht convergence criteria counter-productive to the overall success of monetary union and said the president's "insistent and penetrating" speeches made Germans unpopular.

The Bundesbank spokesman said Schmidt made the same accusations in a letter to Die Zeit in April 1996 and that Tietmeyer had responded in a personal letter to Schmidt, which the newspaper also published.

The spokesman said that in that letter Tietmeyer had said he was not an opponent of monetary union in Europe and had been an emphatic supporter of it ever since his membership of the Werner committee on European monetary union in 1970.
